info.title: ALTR — Tag-based governance policy on Databricks
info.description:
This is an alpha API and may be changed or removed entirely in the future.

After registering your Databricks service principal and workspace with ALTR using `POST /databases` in the [Management API](https://altrnet.live.altr.com/api/swagger/#/databases/createDatabase), use this API to define tag-based governance on tagged columns in Databricks.

Your ALTR organization must be explicitly enable to use this API. Contact ALTR support.

tags.name: Databricks Tag Policy
tags.description: Operations related to applying tag-based governance policies to Databricks

post.summary: Start application of a tag-based policy
post.description:
When `policyAction` is `set`, an asynchronous Databricks job is launched to apply the given `policy` on all columns tagged with `tagName`.

When `policyAction` is set to `delete`, `policy` is ignored, and a Databricks job is launched to remove policy configured on tag `tagName`.

In either case, the status of the job can be tracked with the `GET` endpoint using the returned `id`.

id.description: Use this ID in the `GET` request to check the status of the asynchronous application.

400.description: Something is wrong with the request.

401.description: Your API key or secret is wrong or revoked.

403.description: Your ALTR organization is not authorized for this feature.

500.description: Something went wrong server-side. Try again later.

get.summary: Get status and logs of a tag-based policy application
get.description:
Check status of an asynchronous application of a tag-based policy started in the `POST` endpoint.

Returns the status and, if available, a presigned S3 URL to the logs.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the tag-based policy application as provided in the `POST` response

200.description:
Successfully retrieved status of given tag-based policy asynchronous application, and the application is in a final state, so logs are available.

Note the given pre-signed URL is valid for *at most* one hour. If it expires, try this request again, and you will get a new pre-signed URL.

status.description: Current status of the application of the tag-based policy.

statusMsg.example: Successfully applied tag-based ALTR governance policy!
statusMsg.description: Message, if any, included along with current status.

lastStatusUpdateTime.description: Most recent time the status of the given application has been updated.

presignedS3HttpMethod.description: HTTP method to use when fetch the logs from S3.

presignedS3Url.description: URL to use when fetch the logs from S3.

presignedS3Headers.description: HTTP headers to use when fetch the logs from S3.

202.description: Successfully retrieved status of given tag-based policy asynchronous application, and that asynchronous operation is not yet done.

status.description: Current status of the application of the tag-based policy. Logs are not available while the status is `pending`

statusMsg.description: Message, if any, included along with current status.

lastStatusUpdateTime.description: Most recent time the status of the given application has been updated.

400.description: Something is wrong with the request.

401.description: Your API key or secret is wrong or revoked.

403.description: Your ALTR organization is not authorized for this feature.

basicAuth.description:
Use ALTR API Key authentication.

On the ALTRnet, go to `Settings/Preferences/API/Add New`. - The `Username:` below is `API Key Name/Username` (e.g., `ALTR-6B12A4565...`) - The `Password:` below is `API Key Secret/Password`.

PolicyActionEnum.description:
Specifies whether to set or remove policy from columns with the given `tagName`. Possible values are:
- `set`: Set the policy on the given `tagName` to the given `policy`; any policy previously on this `tagName` is discarded.
- `delete`: Remove all policy on all columns with this `tagName`.

StatusEnum.description:
Specifies what state the job to apply the policy is in. Possible values are:
- `pending`: The request to apply policy has been received, and the job to apply it is running.
- `applied`: The job is done, and the requested action (`set` or `delete`) has been applied.
- `errored`: Some aspect of the job errored. There could be no policy applied or partial policy applied.

MaskActionEnum.description:
Specifies what to do to the value in governed column. Possible values are:
- `none`: No action. (Equivalent to `allow`). When a column has the given `tagName`, but none of the `rules` apply, `none` is used for the `defaultAction`.
- `null_out`: Replace with `null`.
- `last_four`: Excepting hyphens and other group "separators", replace every character except the final four with `*`.
- `full_mask`: Replace every character with `*`.
- `allow`: Allow the value as is. (Equivalent to `none`).
- `constant_mask`: Replace the entire value with the constant value of `****`.
- `email_mask`: Replace every character before the final `@` with `*`.

credentialsId.description: The `id` received from ALTR when your Databricks service principal was registered using the ALTR [Management API](https://altrnet.live.altr.com/api/swagger/#/databases/createDatabase).

tagName.description: Any column tagged with a tag named this case-*in*sensitive `tagName` will have policy applied.

roles.description: The user executing this query must be a member of any of these roles ("groups" in Databricks) for this rule to apply.

tagValues.description: The *value* of the tag named `tagName` on this column must have one of these case-sensitive values for this rule to apply.

permissivity.description: If multiple rules match at query-time, the rule with the highest `permissivity` is applied. If multiple rules match with the same permissivity, one of them will randomly be applied, so be very careful when setting your `permissivity` values.
